title: The Eternal Fool's Words of Wisdom: A Pawsitively Fantastic Adventure Anime Unveils Main Trailer, January 9 Premiere, Additional Cast, Theme Songs
content:
The Eternal Fool’s Words of Wisdom: A Pawsitively Fantastic Adventure anime TV anime unveiled a main trailer and is officially set to begin broadcasting on January 9, 2027, on TOKYO MX, BS Asahi, AT-X and other channels. Crunchyroll will stream the series and the simulcast schedule will be announced on a later date.

Rie Kugimiya also joins the cast as the voice of Aileen. A new character visual and an official comment from Kugimiya have also been released:

“I’m Rie Kugimiya, and I’ll be voicing Aileen. She may look cute and delicate, but she’s actually quite a bit older than she appears and is an incredibly strong character in more ways than one! I’m putting everything I’ve got into the role so I can match her powerful personality. The series is full of fun interactions between its many characters, and I hope you’ll look forward to watching it!”

Additionally, the opening and ending theme songs for the TV anime have been revealed. The opening theme song is “321 Smiling” by Nako Misaki × sajou no hana, while the ending theme song is “Mirai no Vision” by ARCANA PROJECT. Comments from the artists have also been released.

Nako Misako’s comment:

“Hello, I’m Nako Misaki, and I’m delighted to be performing the theme song for the TV anime “The Eternal Fool’s Words of Wisdom: A Pawsitively Fantastic Adventure.” I had the pleasure of singing “321 Smiling” together with sana from sajou no hana. Just like Asley and Pochi, I felt as though I was setting off on an adventure with a trusted partner by my side as I sang alongside sana. I hope the song’s energy, like a refreshing wind pushing you forward, and the excitement of setting out on an adventure will reach everyone who listens. I’m really looking forward to watching the anime myself!”

Comment from sajou no hana:

“After reading the original story, I was really touched by the relationship between Asley and Pochi. They’re always by each other’s side as if it’s the most natural thing in the world. They may argue from time to time, but whenever one of them is in trouble, the other is always there to help. We wanted to capture the feelings that come from their unique bond and the charm of their partnership through upbeat music and lyrics. We hope everyone watching the anime will start each episode with a big smile as soon as they hear the countdown, ‘3, 2, 1!'”

Comment from ARCANA PROJECT:

“We’re truly honored to be performing the ending theme song for the TV anime “The Eternal Fool’s Words of Wisdom: A Pawsitively Fantastic Adventure”! Even when things don’t go as planned, ordinary days can turn into special adventures when you’re with someone important to you. That’s the positive feeling we wanted to express in “Mirai no Vision,” a song filled with an upbeat and cheerful sound. We hope it makes everyone who listens feel a little more excited about the day ahead. Please enjoy the song along with Asley and Pochi’s journey!”

Staff:

• Original Work: Hifumi

• Original Character Design: Kurihito Muto

• Manga Adaptation & Sub-Character Design: Fuh Araki

• Director：Keisuke Onishi

• Series Composition/Script：Kurasumi Sunayama

• Character Design：Yumiko Mizuno

• Background Art：Hiroshi Izumi/Kaya Aoki

• Art Director：Kaya Aoki

• Color setting,：Yusuke Watanabe

• Director of Photography：Yusaku Murakami

• Sound Director：Yukio Nagasaki

• Sound Effects：Hiromune Kurahashi

• Sound Production：Procen Studio

• Music:Yuri Habuka

• Music Production: Lantis

• Animation Producer：Suguru Shakagori

• Animation Studio：Studio Elle

Cast:

• Toshiyuki Toyonaga as Asley

• Yoko Hikasa as Pochi

• Minori Fujidera as Rina

• Rie Kugimiya as Aileen

Synopsis: After accidentally creating a miraculous potion known as the “Eternity Elixir,” Asley gains a body that never ages. With seemingly endless time on his hands, he spends the next 5,000 years studying and mastering countless Spells and Hexes, eventually becoming an exceptionally powerful Sorcerer capable of wielding long-lost ancient Hexes. Hoping to broaden his horizons, Asley sets out on a journey with his familiar and longtime companion, Pochi. But when he stops to help someone along the way, his life takes an unexpected turn. Now, a 5,000-year-old young man and an 800-year-old dog are about to embark on a new adventure. Overpowered yet a little out of touch, Asley finds himself caught up in a lively coming-of-age fantasy unlike any other! Source: Press Release © Hifumi / Earth Star Entertainment / Yukyu no Gusha Azuri Production Committee

title: The Eternal Fool's Words of Wisdom Anime's New Video Unveils More Cast, Theme Songs, January 9 Debut
content:
The staff for the television anime of Hifumi's The Eternal Fool's Words of Wisdom ( Yūkyū no Gusha Asley no, Kenja no Susume ) novels streamed the main promotional video for the anime on Tuesday. The video announces another cast member and the January 9 premiere date for the anime. It also announces and previews the anime's opening theme song "321 smiling" by Nako Misaki × sajou no hana , and the ending theme song "Mirai no Vision" (Future Vision) by ARCANA PROJECT .

The anime will debut on the Tokyo MX channel on January 9 at 10:00 p.m. (8:00 a.m. EST), on BS Asahi on January 10, and on AT-X on January 12.

Rie Kugimiya joins the cast as Aileen, one of the six leading mages in the world.

J-Novel Club is releasing the novels' manga adaptation under the title The Eternal Fool's Words of Wisdom: A Pawsitively Fantastic Adventure , and it describes the story:

A couple thousand years of solitude would wear down any young man—that is, anyone except Asley, an eternally youthful and eternally foolish sorcerer. After all, he has man's best friend...er, familiar, to keep him company. When his Level 100 canine companion Pochi demands that he get some fresh air for the first time in two centuries, Asley sets out to reintegrate into society and test his magic mettle. His mission? Dropping several unglamorous titles from his repertoire and restoring his good (okay, decent) name. A brand-new world and fresh adventures await Asley after his many years of hermitage. Perhaps he'll lend Pochi a hand to place first in the mysterious Familiar Feud. Or maybe he'll lose all vestiges of dignity and turn tail. Whichever comes first! No matter what, Asley has great evil to fight, a big world to save, and even a little growing up to do...that is, if he can endure Pochi's “friendly advice” along the way!

Toshiyuki Toyonaga will star in the anime as Asley, and Yōko Hikasa will voice Pochi. Minori Fujidera plays Rina.

Keisuke Ōnishi ( The Healer Who Was Banished From His Party, Is, in Fact, the Strongest ) is directing the series at Studio Elle . Kurasumi Sunayama ( Dr. Stone: Science Future , Harem in the Labyrinth of Another World ) is in charge of the series scripts, and Yumiko Mizuno ( The Healer Who Was Banished From His Party, Is, in Fact, the Strongest ) will design the characters. Yuri Habuka ( Maebashi Witches , Sushi and Beyond ) is composing the music at Lantis .

Other staff members include:

• Art design, Art Director: Kaya Aoki

• Color Key Artist: Yūsuke Watanabe

• Compositing Director of Photography: Yūsaku Murakami

• Sound Director: Yukio Nagasaki

• Sound Effects: Hiromune Kurahashi

• Sound Production: Procen Studio

• Animation Producer: Suguru Shakagōri

Hifumi began serializing the original story on the Shōsetsuka ni Narō website in January 2015, and ended it in September 2019. Taibundo Publishing released the first print volume in September 2015, with illustrations by Kurihito Mutō , and released the 14th and final volume in December 2019.

Fuh Araki launched the manga adaptation on Earth Star Entertainment 's Comic Earth Star website in April 2017. Earth Star Entertainment shipped the 13th compiled book volume for the manga on February 12. J-Novel Club released the manga's 10th volume in English on September 9. The manga is also available on the Crunchyroll Manga app.

title: Live-Action Twisted Sisters Series Reveals More Cast, January 10 Debut
content:
NHK announced eight more cast members and the January 10 premiere date for the live-action series for Kazumi Yamashita 's Twisted Sisters manga on Tuesday. The new cast members include:

Hiroshi Tachi as Tadashi Ioroi, the father of Tiara, Junko, Rikako, and Ryōko

Jin Shirasu as Raizō Kameishi, the architect of the house where the sisters live

Rui Kurihara as Kotarō Ioroi, Junko's son

Haruki Mochizuki as Ren Yamoto, Tiara's boyfriend

Tomu Miyazaki as Ryūtoku Daimonji, a lawyer and executor of Tadashi's will

Fujiko Kojima as Yuki Yoneyama, an architect under Raizō, and a key person in the second half of the story

Yoshiyuki Tsubokura as Shingo Sakakibara, the editor of the shōjo magazine Frill , where Rikako's manga serializes

Nichika Akutsu as Ken Hosokawa, Rikako's editor for her manga

The series will premiere on the BS and BSP4K channel on January 10.

The series follows manga artist Rikako, who reunites with her estranged sisters over their dying father's will. The will demands the five sisters live together in a mansion and she discovers a secret sister she's never met.

The cast includes (pictured right, from left to right):

• Yumia Fujisaki as Tiara Ioroi

• Hikari Ishida as Junko Ioroi

• Miori Takimoto as Rikako Ioroi

• Hisako Manda as Ryōko Ioroi

Masao Iketani and Tomomi Maruyama will co-write the screenplay. Takashi Ninomiya will direct the series.

Yamashita launched the manga in Kodansha 's Morning magazine in June 2021. Kodansha shipped the ninth compiled book volume on January 22. The 10th volume will ship on Thursday.

Yamashita launched the Land manga on Kodansha 's Morning magazine March 2014, and ended it in July 2020. Kodansha shipped the 11th and final volume in September 2020. Yen Press publishes the series in English.

Yen Press is also publishing Yamashita's Wonder Boy manga in English.

title: Live-Action My Sister's Boyfriend Film's New Video Highlights Song by timelesz
content:
The official website for My Sister's Boyfriend , the live-action film of Amu Meguro 's Midori Loves My Sister ( Onē-chan no Midori-kun or literally My sister's Midori-kun ) manga, presented a new special video for the film on Tuesday. The video features the film's theme song "Hontō no Koto o Iu to" (If I Tell the Truth) by the group timelesz .

The original manga centers on Sui, a girl in her third year of junior high. She doesn't really get along with her older sister's boyfriend, Midori-kun, since he always treats her like a kid and makes fun of her. But Midori-kun is suddenly asked to be Sui's home tutor, and she suddenly sees an unexpected side of him.

The film has the English title My Sister's Boyfriend , and stars timelesz idol group member Masaki Hashimoto (live-action Summer Complicity ) as Midori Yukishiro, and actress Runa Nakajima (live-action Uchi no Otōto-domo ga Sumimasen ) as Sui Sanae. Rinka Kumada (live-action Otonanajimi , Kimi ni Todoke , It Takes More than a Pretty Face to Fall in Love ) plays Sui's older sister and Midori's girlfriend Momo Sanae, and Reo Matsumoto (live-action I Cannot Reach You , Propaganda Game ) plays Sui's childhood friend Ayame Mizukawa. Taisuke Niihara (live-action At 25:00 in Akasaka , Young & Fine ) plays Amamiya, a new assistant producer at the same TV station where Sui's older sister Momo works.

Mahito Kimura (live-action Strobe Edge , Blue Spring Ride series) is directing the film, and Nami Kikkawa (live-action Honey Lemon Soda film) wrote the script. Shochiku is credited for planning and overseeing the production, and is also distributing the film. timelesz performs the film's theme song "Hontō no Koto o Iu to" (If I Tell the Truth).

The film will open in Japan on December 4.

Meguro launched the manga in Shueisha 's Bessatsu Margaret magazine in 2022. Shueisha published the manga's 11th compiled book volume on April 23.

Meguro ended the Hinata no Blue manga in July 2021. Meguro launched the manga in Bessatsu Margaret in April 2019.

Meguro's Honey So Sweet manga ran in Bessatsu Margaret from August 2012 to November 2015. Viz Media 's Shojo Beat imprint has released the eight-volume manga in English. The series was ranked as one of Japanese Bookstore Employees' top recommended comics for 2014. The manga inspired a live-action film adaptation that opened in Japan in March 2018.

title: 5 Dark Fantasy Anime to Watch on Crunchyroll in November 2026
content:
The ever-growing popularity of the anime industry has many enthusiasts looking to venture into the world of exciting series. However, considering the number of series out there, with many of them being long-running or having multiple seasons, choosing the right series can be quite overwhelming. Not to mention that a large portion of the famous shows are actually battle shonen series, but the world of anime is way more vast than that. Dark fantasies, especially those with thought-provoking themes and genre-defining plots, are often overlooked despite having the potential to be industry hits. Such stories are complex, without loud action that draws most viewers in.

The Fall 2026 anime season kicked off last month, and all major platforms, especially Crunchyroll, have released exciting new shows for fans across the globe. Crunchyroll by far had the biggest anime lineup for the season, just like every other quarter, with new weekly releases to keep fans busy for the rest of the year. However, since the latest season’s anime was released only released last month, there aren’t enough episodes for fans to binge. If you’re looking for new anime shows to watch this month that have already released full seasons, then this list is perfect for you.

5) Re:Zero -Starting Life in Another World-

Not only is it one of the most famous anime exclusively available on Crunchyroll, but it is also one of the highest-rated isekai of all time. The anime series is based on the acclaimed light novel written by Tappei Nagatsuki and illustrated by Shinichiro Ootsuka. Two years after the novel debuted in 2016, the White Fox animation studio released the anime adaptation, which continues to return with new sequels. 2026 marks the 10th anniversary of the anime, and over all these years, four seasons have been released, as the story keeps getting more intense.

The anime is often praised for exciting plot twists, unique worldbuilding, and thrilling action as it centers around Subaru Natsuki, an ordinary teenage boy. After leaving a convenience store one evening, he suddenly finds himself transported into another world. Equipped with the ability to return to time, Subaru tries his best to adjust to the new world while also dealing with any threat that comes his way.

4) Dorohedoro

This dark fantasy from MAPPA is based on an older manga which was serialized from 2000 to 2018. The anime shares strong aesthetic ties with gritty details while following a hyper-violent Japanese animation that’s reminiscent of the 1990s. The story takes place in an underground alley called the Hole, which draws heavily from the grimy, pipe-filled, rain-slicked urban dystopias seen in 90s cyberpunk and Seinen anime such as Ghost in the Shell: Memories or Battle Angel Alita . The animation style uses 2D and 3D CG by the studio, but the design philosophy and aesthetics aren’t that different from the cult spirit of the 1990s animation.

The anime debuted in 2000, and it took MAPPA six years to return with a second season this year. A third season has already been confirmed , and fans are awaiting updates on the anime as Caiman and Nikaido get closer to discovering the dark secrets lingering in the alleys of the Hole while also uncovering what transpired in the past.

3) Puella Magi Madoka Magica

Puella Magi Madoka Magica is an acclaimed fantasy classic on Crunchyroll with a surprise dark twist beneath its cheerful facade. The story focuses on magical girls and remains one of the most shocking series of all time. The award-winning show released its anime adaptation in 2011 before returning with sequel films in 2012 and 2013. This acclaimed original series follows Madoka Kaname and Sayaka Miki, two middle school girls whose ordinary lives take drastic turns after encountering Kyuubey, a mysterious magical familiar. Kyuubey offers the girls an offer to grant any one of their wishes if they become magical girls.

The girls can gain enough power to fulfill their dreams. However, Homura Akemi, a new transfer student and a magical girl, tries her best to stop them from accepting the offer. She claims that the offer isn’t what it looks like, implying there will be a major price to pay.

2) Sentenced to Be a Hero

However, among the major titles of the season, a new action fantasy series quickly climbed the ranks. Sentenced to Be a Hero caused huge waves in the anime industry after its debut on Crunchyroll as it captured fans’attention with its spectacular animation, unique premise, and promising plot. The anime is not only highly rated but also offers a lot of unique concepts, which make it stand out from the rest. The anime series is based on a light novel written by Rocket Shoukai and illustrated by Mephisto.

This dark fantasy story offers a twisted outlook on the role of a hero since this title is given only to those who have committed the most heinous crimes. While almost all fantasy stories glorify the coveted title of hero, this anime considers it the worst punishment anyone can ever receive. Heroes are those who serve in the military in an endless war against the Demon Lords. However, the worst part is that the convicts aren’t even allowed to die. If they somehow lose their lives in the battle, they will be resurrected over and over again, so they will keep fighting a never-ending war. The resurrection process is brutal since it forces the soul of a hero straight out of hell and puts it back into its corpse.

1) Attack on Titan

When it comes to modern anime, specifically those released in the 2010s and 2020s, Attack on Titan ‘s legacy can’t be matched with anything else. Written and illustrated by Hajime Isayama, the manga reached its controversial finale in 2021, which sparked so much fury from fans that the creator was losing sleep over it. Attack on Titan follows Eren Yeager, a boy whose mother is devoured by a Titan when monstrous, humanoid beings breach his hometown’s walls.

This trauma ignites a burning obsession to destroy every Titan. What starts as a survival horror story quickly transforms into political intrigue. title: Attack on Titan Doesn’t Need a Comeback After Its Perfect Ending
content:
When it comes to modern anime, specifically those released in the 2010s and 2020s, Attack on Titan ‘s legacy can’t be matched with anything else. Written and illustrated by Hajime Isayama, the manga reached its controversial finale in 2021, which sparked so much fury from fans that the creator was losing sleep over it. However, the controversy didn’t last for long when MAPPA took over the anime series for the final season. Although WIT Studio worked on the first three seasons of the anime, it faced difficulty meeting the tight deadlines since the manga was already over. It didn’t take long for MAPPA to take over the helm, and that probably saved the franchise’s legacy.

Established in 2011, MAPPA is known as one of the most renowned animation studios in Japan. While its popularity skyrocketed in the 2020s with the release of Jujutsu Kaisen and a few other acclaimed shows, the studio had a strong foundation with exceptional shows and movies under its belt ever since its establishment. Fans naturally had high expectations from the studio for the final season, especially since the time-skip changed the entire narrative. MAPPA not only lived up to the expectations, but delivered the best possible version of the story in the final season and special episodes. The anime reached its conclusion on November 4th, 2023, with the release of the second special episode of Attack on Titan: Final Season – The Final Chapters .

Attack on Titan Is More Widely Accepted After Its Controversial Ending

The final stretch of the manga sparked numerous controversies with nuanced scenes that not many appreciated, as well as the death of beloved characters. The ending became less hated despite having reasonable detractors after the anime adaptation , since a few years had passed by then, and the original scenes soothed fans’ disappointment. The problem with cynical or analytical endings is that not everyone will perceive them in the same way. Additionally, Mikasa kissing Eren’s severed head should’ve been an emotional moment of the story, but it didn’t have the impact it should’ve because of its off-putting execution.

The cycle never truly ended in the series, leaving room for a sequel or a spin-off, but the creator has yet to return with a new story. Several decades after Eren’s death, Paradis is still destroyed, and a young boy with a dog discovers the tree where Eren was buried, which now has the same appearance as the tree where Ymir gained the power of the Titans. The implication is that the boy may gain the abilities of a Titan, thereby bringing that destructive power into the world again. Hence, there’s a strong possibility that the current world remains at risk of going through everything all over again, implying that peace is not everlasting.

Attack on Titan ‘s Ending Perfect Ending Leaves No Room for a Sequel

Considering how much fans hated the finale when the manga was being serialized, not many expected that the controversy would completely die down after the anime adaptation. Isayama was also involved in the production and worked closely with the anime staff to refine dialogue and certain moments while subtly adding original scenes. He also helped tweak many scenes to make the emotional beats land more sincerely than they did in the manga. The anime didn’t make major changes from the original, but these minor details and the presentation with stunning animation made a world of difference.

This not only made fans forget their initial dissatisfaction with the manga, but also helped the series reach new heights of global popularity. The anime was well-received thanks to all the efforts of the studio and the creator. Despite taking the torch from WIT Studio during a controversial moment and the tight deadlines, MAPPA’s adaptation saved the series with one of the best adaptations in recent years. Since Isayama didn’t work on any extra chapter or spin-off, there won’t be another anime episode or movie with a completely new story.

However, that doesn’t mean the end of the franchise since both WIT Studio and MAPPA keep returning with new projects and merchandise to keep fans intrigued.Its final chapters drive home its powerful — albeit bleak — message about the cycle of violence and human nature. And it gives the series and its characters an epic send-off from the beginning of Season 4. There’s tons of well-animated action, along with great callbacks to prior chapters and incredible character growth. It’s everything you could want in a finale, and it doesn’t deserve all the hate it gets.

Do you think MAPPA delivered the perfect ending for Attack on Titan ? What moment from the finale made the biggest impression on you? Share your thoughts in the comments below!

title: Tetsuya Tsutsui Launches New Ortrans Manga
content:
This year's 50th issue of Shueisha 's Young Jump magazine announced on November 12 that Tetsuya Tsutsui will launch a new series titled Ortrans in next year's eighth issue on January 21.

The story revolves around a series of disappearances of children from a juvenile training school. Two detectives on the case discover a disturbing video that seems to be related to the case.

Tsutsui launched the Neeting Life manga on Shueisha 's YanJan! app and on the Tonari no Young Jump website in December 2021, and ended it in January 2023.

Tsutsui launched the noise manga (pictured right) in Grand Jump in December 2017, and ended it in January 2020. Shueisha published the manga's third and final compiled book volume in March 2020. The manga inspired a live-action film that opened in Japan in January 2022.

Tsutsui launched the Prophecy ( Yokokuhan ) manga in Shueisha 's Jump X magazine in 2011, and ended it in August 2013. Shueisha published three volumes for the manga. Vertical published all three volumes. Fumio Obata launched a spinoff manga titled Yokokuhan: The Copycat in Jump X in April 2014, and ended it in 2015. The manga also received three volumes. Prophecy inspired a live-action film that opened in Japan in June 2015.

title: Dragon Ball Super Needs to Bring Back Frieza’s Full Family
content:
Frieza has been the lone constant villain since Dragon Ball Z , and with the evil emperor still alive in the timeline, it’s time to bring his entire family into the fight. Some villains might boast more strength than him, but Frieza is the most dynamic, proving that he can build upon his powers while maintaining his relentless ruthlessness . He was wished back to life by Goku in order to help the Z Fighters win the Tournament of Power for Universe 7. The wish proved successful as Universe 7 ended up winning, but it obviously came at a cost of Frieza being alive and well.

The only logical next step for him would be to try and destroy his longtime nemesis Goku. In order to do that, he’ll need a lot of help considering the Frieza Force troop’s losses over the years. The best way to counter that is to get more high-tier fighters, which is where his family comes into play. King Cold is already a part of the current canon, but probably needs some significant power boosting after his decimation at the hands of Future Trunks. Next, it’s time to introduce Cooler to the Dragon Ball canon and really up the ante.

Cooler Waited Years For This

Frieza’s older brother is like the non-Saiyan version of the original Broly. First introduced 35 years ago in the Dragon Ball Z film Cooler’s Revenge , he’s in a lot of content, but all of it is now non-canon. Unlike his brother’s final form, Cooler’s masked face and towering physique make him a much more imposing fighter. Cooler recently achieved the Golden Cooler form in Super Dragon Ball Heroes , so the concept is out there that he can compete with this new godly level of Saiyan power in the later releases.

Cooler provides an immediate power up to his brother’s forces. However, he’s not the only member of the family that can fight. King Cold, their father, built an empire on conquering worlds and destroying civilizations. His minimal appearances don’t show off his skills, and his quick defeat in the lone battle he fought in undersells his skills. He’s currently dead but probably got plenty of training in the afterlife, as he’s currently in hell for his many vile acts. If Frieza brings him back, that family trio would definitely give the Z Fighters some problems.

Dragon Ball Manga Adds More To Frieza’s Powers

The most recent on-screen appearance for Frieza came in Dragon Ball Super: Broly , but he’s not sat idly by since taking a beating from the Legendary Super Saiyan. The Dragon Ball Super manga displays an even more powerful version of the villain. Frieza unveils that he found a hyperbolic time chamber that allowed him to further expand his powers and become Black Frieza in the Granolah the Survivor Saga . He defeats Goku and Vegeta easily and moves on.

His powered-up form combined with Golden Cooler, and just for fun, a transformed King Cold would provide maybe the toughest trio for Goku, Vegeta and friends to battle. Frieza is the only bad guy with the same tenacity as the Saiyan heroes and that’s why even though he continually loses, his threat always looms large. The setup is there for him and his family to get a shot at revenge. Do you think they should get another shot at the Saiyans? Would you want to see the Frieza family return? Let us know in the comments.

title: D.I.C.E. Awards Honors Nintendo Game Creator Shigeru Miyamoto With Inaugural Legend Award
content:
According to the AIAS, the Legend Award recognizes "an industry icon whose enduring vision continues to redefine interactive entertainment," and celebrates the impact and influence of "creators whose groundbreaking achievements have already earned lasting universal acclaim."

Miyamoto is the main designer of the first incarnations of some of Nintendo 's most celebrated, well-known, and long-running game franchises, including Mario Bros. , Donkey Kong , The Legend of Zelda , Pikmin , and Star Fox , and continued to be a main designer for some of those franchise 's later games. He also helped shape the concept behind the Wii, one of Nintendo 's most successful console platforms. He has the title of Representative Director and Creative Fellow at Nintendo .

Japan's Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology announced on October 22 the eight recipients for this year's prestigious Order of Culture award, and Nintendo game designer Miyamoto has become the first person in the gaming industry to receive the honor. The order is awarded to those "who have made outstanding contributions in developing" Japanese culture. The Emperor presented Miyamoto with the award on November 3, Japan's Culture Day. At a press conference at Nintendo in Kyoto, Miyamoto stated that as games are created by not just one person, but by many collaborating together, he honors their work with this award.

Miyamoto earned Japan's Person of Cultural Merit honor in 2019. He also earned Spain's prestigious Prince of Asturias Award in the category of Communications and Humanities in 2012.

Nintendo composer Kōji Kondō ( Super Mario Bros. , The Legend of Zelda ) earned the Hall of Fame award at the D.I.C.E. Awards in 2024.

At the 29th Annual D.I.C.E. Awards earlier this year, Death Stranding 2: On the Beach won the awards for "Outstanding Achievement in Audio Design" and "Outstanding Technical Achievement." Persona 5 : The Phantom X won "Mobile Game of the Year," and Mario Kart World won "Racing Game of the Year."

title: Here’s Where My Hero Academia’s Anime Really Went Wrong
content:
There’s no denying My Hero Academia is one of the most successful anime and manga franchises of all time. However, even with all the exceptional talents working to help the anime become a worldwide success, the adaptation can’t be said to be perfect. While the manga ended its serialization in August 2024, the anime wrapped up the main story in December last year. Following the emotional final season, the anime returned with a special episode to adapt the extra chapter from the final volume and also released a short following Eri’s story after the time-skip . Regardless of the controversial manga finale, fans had nothing but praise for the anime’s conclusion, even though Studio Bones didn’t change anything from the source material.

However, the anime’s earlier seasons weren’t adapted nearly as well as the final season. This isn’t simply about the visuals, but also how much the adaptation followed the main source. Season 5 is often considered the weakest season in the series due to the fact that the early episodes mostly focused on the U.A. students and the Joint Training Arc. Towards the second cour of the season, it adapted the My Villain Academia Arc, also known as the Meta Liberation Army Arc , which was ruined due to several factors.

My Hero Academia Season 5 Made Several Changes to My Villain Academia

The fifth season was the calm before the storm when the Meta Liberation Army was just preparing for the war against the heroes. During the My Villain Academia Arc, the story’s focus shifted completely to the League of Villains and their conflict with the Meta Liberation Army. However, fans were shocked by the number of changes made by the anime. The series not only took out a lot of character depth from characters such as Spinner and Re-Destro but also toned down the intense violence shown in the manga.

Horikoshi is known for his gritty art style with intricate details and bloody violence. He doesn’t shy away from highlighting the brutality of the hero society, but the anime adaptation often needs to worry about censorship, especially if it’s going to be broadcast on television. The manga was far more brutal during Shigaraki’s present and past in this arc. This is especially the case when it featured Garaki performing painful experiments on Shigaraki, where the manga made the scene look so much more disturbing.

The story itself doesn’t change much, but the way that the anime toned down the gritty details makes it much less impactful. We also can’t forget how Re-Destro wasn’t as fleshed out in the anime since the manga not only featured more of his backstory but also highlighted his violent and psychotic nature when it came to the goals of Destro. Additionally, Spinner’s origin was the most crucial part of his character writing, but the anime didn’t dive deeper into his mindset when he joined the League of Villains. A lot of his inner monologue was missing from the anime that made his origin story less memorable.

My Hero Academia Season 5 Suffered From the Movie Promotion

My Hero Academia has released four non-canon movies , all of which were unarguably major successes across the box office and streaming services. The animation studio often worked with Horikoshi for the story and the character designs to ensure that fans wouldn’t be disappointed with the release. My Hero Academia: World Heroes’ Mission was released when the anime was still airing its fifth season. This is why Studio Bones swapped the Endeavor Agency arc and the My Villain Academia arc to sync with the theatrical release of the movie.

The anime suffered from the jumbled-up arcs and the pacing issues while also reducing the tension of the story, especially for anime-only fans. My Villain Academia ran for 23 chapters in the manga, but the anime condensed it to six episodes, which severely rushed things for the villains. This is a huge difference compared to the Joint Training Arc, which ran for 24 chapters but was adapted into 10 episodes in the anime.

Since the Endeavor Agency Arc aired before My Villain Academia, fans already knew that the League of Villains fought against the Meta Liberation Army and survived. This is something that the manga didn’t reveal until the fight was over, as it kept building up the tension since the battle between villain organizations could have been in anyone’s favor. contentBlocks.text: There’s no denying My Hero Academia is one of the most successful anime and manga franchises of all time. However, even with all the exceptional talents working to help the anime become a worldwide success, the adaptation can’t be said to be perfect. While the manga ended its serialization in August 2024, the anime wrapped up the main story in December last year. Following the emotional final season, the anime returned with a special episode to adapt the extra chapter from the final volume and also released a short following Eri’s story after the time-skip . Regardless of the controversial manga finale, fans had nothing but praise for the anime’s conclusion, even though Studio Bones didn’t change anything from the source material.

However, the anime’s earlier seasons weren’t adapted nearly as well as the final season. This isn’t simply about the visuals, but also how much the adaptation followed the main source. Season 5 is often considered the weakest season in the series due to the fact that the early episodes mostly focused on the U.A. students and the Joint Training Arc. Towards the second cour of the season, it adapted the My Villain Academia Arc, also known as the Meta Liberation Army Arc , which was ruined due to several factors.
My Hero Academia Season 5 Made Several Changes to My Villain Academia

The fifth season was the calm before the storm when the Meta Liberation Army was just preparing for the war against the heroes. During the My Villain Academia Arc, the story’s focus shifted completely to the League of Villains and their conflict with the Meta Liberation Army. However, fans were shocked by the number of changes made by the anime. The series not only took out a lot of character depth from characters such as Spinner and Re-Destro but also toned down the intense violence shown in the manga.

Horikoshi is known for his gritty art style with intricate details and bloody violence. He doesn’t shy away from highlighting the brutality of the hero society, but the anime adaptation often needs to worry about censorship, especially if it’s going to be broadcast on television. The manga was far more brutal during Shigaraki’s present and past in this arc. This is especially the case when it featured Garaki performing painful experiments on Shigaraki, where the manga made the scene look so much more disturbing.

The story itself doesn’t change much, but the way that the anime toned down the gritty details makes it much less impactful. We also can’t forget how Re-Destro wasn’t as fleshed out in the anime since the manga not only featured more of his backstory but also highlighted his violent and psychotic nature when it came to the goals of Destro. Additionally, Spinner’s origin was the most crucial part of his character writing, but the anime didn’t dive deeper into his mindset when he joined the League of Villains. A lot of his inner monologue was missing from the anime that made his origin story less memorable.
My Hero Academia Season 5 Suffered From the Movie Promotion

My Hero Academia has released four non-canon movies , all of which were unarguably major successes across the box office and streaming services. The animation studio often worked with Horikoshi for the story and the character designs to ensure that fans wouldn’t be disappointed with the release. My Hero Academia: World Heroes’ Mission was released when the anime was still airing its fifth season. This is why Studio Bones swapped the Endeavor Agency arc and the My Villain Academia arc to sync with the theatrical release of the movie.

The anime suffered from the jumbled-up arcs and the pacing issues while also reducing the tension of the story, especially for anime-only fans. My Villain Academia ran for 23 chapters in the manga, but the anime condensed it to six episodes, which severely rushed things for the villains. This is a huge difference compared to the Joint Training Arc, which ran for 24 chapters but was adapted into 10 episodes in the anime.
